e.etymology: A respelling of Berkeley, an English surname and place name from Old English beorc and leah, 'birch wood or clearing'.

assoc.t: Berklee College of Music in Boston

e.etymology: From an English surname taken from a small place in Devon, Old English for 'the farmstead of a man named Lugga'. Its recent rise follows Lux and the -ton names such as Paxton and Jaxton.
For girls, the Hebrew name of King Saul's daughter, the first wife of David; it may be a form of Michael, 'who is like God?', or mean 'brook'. For boys, the Czech and Slovak form of Michael.
e.note: Often misread as Michael or Michelle.

e.meaning: Christmas Day, birthday of the Lord
e.etymology: A spelling of Natalie, the French form of the Late Latin saint's name Natalia, from natalis dies, 'birthday', meaning the birthday of Christ.
The Polish, Russian and Serbian spelling of Alexandra, the feminine of Greek Alexandros, from alexein, 'to defend', and aner, 'man'.
A given name from the surname Rustin, taken up in the 1970s alongside Dustin and Justin and as a longer form of Rusty.
namesakes: Rustin Cohle (detective Rust Cohle in HBO's True Detective)

assoc.t: Rustin, 2023 film about activist Bayard Rustin

e.etymology: A respelling of Talia said tuh-LEE-uh. Talia is Hebrew Talya, 'dew of God', and also a short form of Natalia.
The Somali form of Arabic Abd al-Rahman, 'servant of the Most Merciful'. Al-Rahman is one of the names of God in the Quran; Somali regularly turns Abdul- names into Abdi-.
A spelling of Carmelo, the Italian and Spanish men's name taken from Mount Carmel in Israel, Hebrew karmel, 'garden' or 'orchard', and from the title Our Lady of Mount Carmel.

assoc.t: Carmelo Anthony, NBA star known as Melo (same sound)

e.etymology: From Irish Aine, written with an accent on the A, from Old Irish an, 'bright, splendid'. In Irish legend Aine is a goddess of summer and sovereignty linked with County Limerick.
e.note: Said AWN-yuh in Irish; Americans who do not know the name may read it as AYN.

e.etymology: A spelling of Ulises, the Spanish form of Ulysses, the Latin name of Odysseus, the wandering hero of Homer's Odyssey. The meaning of the Greek name is uncertain.
A form of Johanna, the feminine of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, 'God is gracious'. The Y spelling is used in Latin America, Ethiopia, Eritrea and Indonesia; in Swahili Yohana is the men's name John.
No settled source; it sits beside Keon and Kian. Its US use rose after Disney's The Lion Guard (2015) gave the name to Simba's son, the lion cub hero.

assoc.t: Kion, Simba's son and hero of Disney's The Lion Guard

e.etymology: A modern American coinage that puts the Za- opening on the -miyah ending shared by Jamiyah, Samiyah and Amiyah.

e.meaning: devout, one who turns from worldly things
e.etymology: From Arabic zahid, an ascetic: a person who gives up worldly comforts for a life of devotion. It is used across the Muslim world, from Pakistan to Indonesia.

e.meaning: not dual; one without a second
e.etymology: From Sanskrit advaita, not two. The word names Advaita Vedanta, the school of Hindu philosophy that holds the self and ultimate reality to be one.
From the English word shine, Old English scinan, to give off light. It is a recent American word name, and also an English surname.
e.note: Shine was once a racial slur for a Black person; the usage is dated but not forgotten.

e.etymology: An Arabic name from the root n-s-b, which has to do with lineage and kinship. It honors Nusaybah bint Ka'ab, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad remembered for shielding him in battle at Uhud.
From Hebrew elyon, highest. In the Hebrew Bible El Elyon, God Most High, is a title of God; its use as a personal name is recent.
A blend of Leo and Giovanni, the Italian form of John. It is used mostly by Hispanic families in the United States, alongside Geovanni and Jiovanni.

e.meaning: woodland clearing, from a place name in Cheshire
e.etymology: A respelling of Huxley, an English surname from a place in Cheshire: Old English leah, a woodland clearing, after an uncertain first part, perhaps a man's name. Aldous Huxley, author of Brave New World, made it famous.
In the US mostly a pet form or offshoot of Nova, from Latin novus, new. In Indonesia Novi is a separate name often given to girls born in November.

assoc.t: Novi, Michigan, a suburb of Detroit

e.etymology: A German pet form of Margarete (Margaret), from Grete plus the diminutive -chen: little Greta. Margaret goes back to Greek margarites, pearl. Goethe's Faust made the name famous.

assoc.t: Gretchen Wieners of Mean Girls (stop trying to make fetch)
Gretchen, the tragic heroine of Goethe's Faust

e.etymology: A spelling of Dwayne or Duane, from the Irish name Dubhán, a diminutive of dubh, dark or black. The De- spelling was at its most popular in the US in the 1960s.
A spelling of Nicole, the French feminine of Nicolas, from Greek Nikolaos: nike, victory, plus laos, people.
namesakes: Nicolle Wallace (MSNBC anchor and former White House aide)

e.etymology: A pet form of David, from Hebrew for beloved. It peaked in the US in 1955 during the Davy Crockett craze, and today it is given to girls nearly as often as boys.

assoc.t: Davy Jones's locker, sailors' name for the sea floor

e.etymology: A respelling of Isaac, from Hebrew Yitzhak, he will laugh. Genesis ties the name to Sarah's laughter on hearing she would bear a son in old age.
From Hebrew Yemimah, dove. In the Book of Job, Jemima is the eldest of the three daughters born to Job after his trials. Puritans took up the name, and it stays in use in Britain.

assoc.t: Aunt Jemima, the pancake brand retired in 2021

e.note: In the US the name is tied to Aunt Jemima, the pancake brand retired in 2021 over its racial stereotype.

e.etymology: An English surname now used as a longer form of Max, in the style of Jaxon and Paxton. Prince Maxon of Kiera Cass's The Selection novels (2012) helped it along.

assoc.t: Prince Maxon in The Selection novels by Kiera Cass

e.etymology: From the Irish surname O'Shea, Ó Séaghdha, descendant of Séaghdha, a byname read as hawk-like or fortunate. Oshea is also the King James Bible's spelling of Hoshea, Joshua's first name.
namesakes: O'Shea Jackson (birth name of rapper and actor Ice Cube)
O'Shea Jackson Jr. (actor, Straight Outta Compton)
